title: AI across the flower business.
name: FiftyFlowers
short: Support, product imagery and company knowledge—connected in one internal platform.
problem: An online flower retailer has very different workflows across customer support, marketing and storefront operations. The challenge is connecting useful AI to each team’s actual information and tools.
contribution: Built and evolved the internal AI platform, support applications, a Chrome extension, marketing tools and commerce integrations. The work spans full-stack application development, cloud services, product-data workflows and visibility into the company’s AI roadmap.
groups: Customer service

Four applications for customer questions, reviews, claims and payment disputes, with shared chat, case history and a Chrome extension. The serving layer moved from AWS Lambda to Firebase and Google Cloud.
Company Second Brain

An umbrella MVP connecting departmental knowledge and tools. Customer Service knowledge, voice and policies support production apps; Marketing demonstrates image-tool guidance and presets; Engineering is a beta used in my own AI-assisted coding.
Marketing workflows

Image Studio supports consistent product photos, reusable presets and transparent cutouts. Farm Exports supports catalog-image work. The FAQ & Content Engine helps identify unanswered questions and review content drafts.
Shopping & operations

The flower-selection assistant, Share Your Flair wedding submissions and urgent-order requests connect storefront interactions with operational workflows. Earlier implementations and later improvements are distinct parts of the work.
Proposal Manager
Implemented supplied wireframes as a tool for event planning, flower recipes, presentations and shopping lists. It was not launched; work paused when DIY Migration took priority.
DIY Kits Migration
Tools match farm spreadsheets with store products and transfer kit recipes and purchase links to a test store, with source tracking and checks. Data cleanup and the production handoff remain ongoing.
Project visibility
A dedicated FiftyFlowers dashboard in The Record, linked from Internal AI, gives access to the AI roadmap, project milestones, completed work and evidence.
next: Continue the migration cleanup and handoff, and develop the company knowledge workspace beyond its MVP. Individual tools have different levels of maturity; the whole platform is not one finished autonomous system.
evidence: Scope reflects the reviewed project records and the saved September 2026 professional profile. The diagram is a capability map, not a screenshot or proof of company-wide adoption.

title: A clearer view of lending decisions.
name: Till
short: Machine-learning loan scoring and an operating dashboard for the lending workflow.
problem: Loan scoring needs to fit into an existing application process, while the team needs visibility into scoring activity and loan performance.
contribution: Built a machine-learning scoring service integrated with the lender’s application system, plus a dashboard for reviewing scoring activity, approval thresholds, lead sources and loan performance.
groups: Scoring integration
Receives application inputs and returns scoring results to the existing lending system.
Operational visibility
Brings scoring activity, policy thresholds, source information and historical performance into one dashboard.
Business outcome
The service saves $2,000 per month, equivalent to $24,000 annualized. The annualized figure expresses the monthly savings over twelve months.
next: Keep scoring behavior, reporting and policy changes understandable as the lending workflow evolves.
evidence: The workflow represents the documented service and dashboard. No customer applications or private financial records are included.

title: Better systems for building systems.
name: AI Development Platform
short: Project management, durable engineering memory and supervised coding-agent workflows.
problem: AI-assisted work can lose context across sessions and scatter decisions across repositories, conversations and tools. Planning and delivery need a shared structure that humans can inspect.
contribution: Built an internal product suite around three distinct responsibilities: managing the work, retaining engineering knowledge and supervising agent assignments. These tools support my own development process; deeper integration remains in development.
groups: The Record · manage the work
A project-management system for developers, clients and connected coding agents. It organizes scoped milestones, progress, decisions and evidence of completed work in a shared workspace.
Brain · preserve the context
Reusable engineering memory for project context, repository knowledge, decisions, workflows and handoffs across coding sessions.
Jarvis OS · coordinate execution
An orchestration prototype for assigning and supervising coding agents. It explores how agent work can connect with the project record and engineering memory.
The working cycle

Plan a bounded milestone, pursue that work, capture questions and evidence, then review the outcome before planning the next scope. Engineering judgment and release accountability stay with the developer.
next: Bring project context and engineering memory into a more unified assistant experience. The complete proposed integration is not presented as a finished autonomous platform.
evidence: This is a conceptual map of the actual product responsibilities. It deliberately omits private prompts, credentials and implementation details.

title: From business reports to useful answers.
name: Create Spaces
short: A reporting workspace connects booking reports, export history and cloud schedule visibility.
problem: Useful sales data lives inside business software. Before a conversational dashboard can be dependable, exports must land somewhere the analysis workflow can actually read.
contribution: Developed the Hedberg bookings-report workflow and a local reporting dashboard connected to private cloud storage. The workspace brings PDF-derived data, saved reports and export status into one interface, while keeping the future conversational layer separate.
groups: Review bookings
The overview presents accepted booking data alongside report coverage and freshness. Figures can be traced back to the source report.
Keep report history
Saved report versions retain their date ranges and source PDF links. Repeated exports remain distinct from newly covered reporting periods.
Inspect the export workflow
The dashboard displays the cloud export schedule, pause control, expandable run history and read-only Booking Report configuration.
Build toward conversation
A conversational AI workspace, editable export frequency and Sync now remain planned.
next: Validate sustained daily reliability and a Mac-off trial. Editable frequency, Sync now and a conversational AI experience remain planned; the dashboard shown here is a working local build, not a public deployment.
evidence: Screenshots captured September 24, 2026 at 10:30 PM Arizona. The working local dashboard is connected to private cloud storage and uses real PDF-derived data.
